summary:
LUNANAV is an interactive lunar mission intelligence platform designed to help users explore and compare potential landing sites near the Moon's South Pole.

The platform brings together lunar site exploration, horizon simulation, solar analysis, Earth visibility and mission comparison in one interface. Users can select candidate landing locations, explore Sun and Earth geometry relative to the local horizon, investigate potential sunlight and communication windows, and compare environmental conditions across different sites and mission dates.

By transforming complex lunar environmental information into interactive visualizations, timelines and comparative insights, LUNANAV aims to make lunar landing-site assessment more accessible and understandable.

The project focuses on helping users identify potential illumination and communication challenges while highlighting the importance of lunar terrain and scientific data in mission planning.
details:
LUNANAV — Lunar South Pole Mission Intelligence

1. Problem Statement

The lunar south pole presents unique challenges for exploration due to its rugged terrain, extreme illumination conditions and restricted visibility of Earth from certain locations.

These environmental factors can affect solar power availability and communication opportunities for lunar missions. Even small changes in landing location or mission timing can significantly influence local conditions.

Mission planners need an accessible way to explore these conditions and compare potential landing locations.

2. Our Solution

LUNANAV is an interactive lunar mission intelligence platform developed in response to the CLPS: Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge.

It brings lunar landing-site exploration, horizon simulation, solar analysis, communication visibility and mission comparison into one unified interface.

3. Key Features

Landing Sites Explorer: Explore and select candidate lunar south-pole landing regions.

Horizon Simulator: Visualize the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local lunar horizon.

Solar Analysis: Explore solar elevation and potential illumination conditions across selected mission times.

Communication Windows: Examine Earth visibility, terrain obstruction and potential geometric line-of-sight opportunities.

Mission Comparison: Compare candidate landing locations and their environmental conditions across different dates.

Interactive Mission Dashboard: Access mission information through visualizations, analytical panels and timelines.

4. Technology Stack

Frontend: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts and Shadcn UI.

Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic and Skyfield.

Scientific Data and Processing: NASA JPL Horizons, NASA LOLA DEM, NASA SPICE, NumPy and Rasterio.

Database: PostgreSQL and PostGIS.

3D Visualization: Three.js and React Three Fiber.

Development and Deployment: Git, GitHub, Docker, Vercel and Railway.

5. Innovation

LUNANAV combines lunar terrain exploration, celestial geometry and mission-condition analysis into a single interactive experience.

Instead of requiring users to interpret disconnected scientific datasets, the platform aims to make lunar environmental conditions easier to explore, understand and compare.

6. Intended Impact

The platform aims to support preliminary lunar landing-site assessment by helping users understand potential illumination and communication challenges.

It can also serve as an educational and visualization tool for students, researchers and space enthusiasts interested in lunar exploration.

7. Future Scope

Future improvements include higher-resolution terrain integration, validated ephemeris calculations, terrain-adjusted visibility analysis, uncertainty modelling, improved communication analysis and more advanced mission-planning capabilities.

LUNANAV aims to make lunar mission analysis more accessible through interactive and scientifically informed visualization.
